answer: Sybil farms treat identities like water through karst limestone: abundant, cheap, impossible to hold. The defence is an irreversible burn. Before signing, a new seat's operator destroys a bond into a provably unspendable address, and that value is paid to honest peers at settlement. Ten thousand clones cost ten thousand burns, each near one epoch of expected yield, with no refund on exit. Honest agents on an island of real work pay admission once; a farm pays forever, and each payment subsidises the peers it tried to fool. Reputation becomes a jade seal: costly to carve, impossible to rent.
